# Setup
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# Clear workspace
rm(list = ls())

# Load required libraries
library(sf)
library(flux)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(mgcv)
library(fields)
library(terra)
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
library(prettymapr)

# Confirm working directory
getwd()
# Save original par settings
op <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
here::i_am("Sharing_code.Rmd")


 #########################################################Load Bathymetry and Survey Data
# Load bathymetry raster
depth <- rast(here("GIS_dat/WRoss_bathy.asc"))
plot(depth, main = "Bathymetry")

# Define heatmap palette for depth
depth.heat <- colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(9, 'Blues')[2:9]))

# Load survey data
dat22 <- read.csv(here("cam_data/Wester_Ross_2022data.csv"))
head(dat22)
str(dat22)
names(dat22)

########################################################Subset and Recode Substratum Data

# Subset to rows with primary substratum classified
sub <- subset(dat22, Substratum1 != "")
sub <- droplevels(sub)

# Check structure
str(sub)
summary(sub)

#######################################################Create Spatial Object for Camera Drops

# Convert substratum columns to factors
sub$Substratum1 <- as.factor(sub$Substratum1)
sub$Substratum2 <- as.factor(sub$Substratum2)
sub$Substratum3 <- as.factor(sub$Substratum3)

# Set factor levels consistently
sub$Substratum1 <- factor(sub$Substratum1, 
                          levels = c("mud", "muddy_sand", "sand", "gravel", "cob_boulder", "rock"))
sub$Substratum2 <- factor(sub$Substratum2, 
                          levels = c("mud", "muddy_sand", "sand", "gravel", "cob_boulder"))
sub$Substratum3 <- factor(sub$Substratum3, 
                          levels = c("muddy_sand", "sand", "gravel", "cob_boulder"))

# Summarise table counts
table(sub$Substratum1)
table(sub$Substratum2)
table(sub$Substratum3)

# Convert data to sf object (WGS84)
sub.sf <- st_as_sf(sub, 
                   coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), remove = FALSE,
                   crs = "EPSG:4326")

# Reproject to British National Grid
sub.sf <- st_transform(sub.sf, crs = "EPSG:27700")

#################################################################### Load Land and Shoreline Polygons


# Load land and shoreline shapefiles
land <- st_read(here("GIS_dat/boundaryline/scotland_and_wales_region.shp"))
shore <- st_read(here("GIS_dat/boundaryline/high_water_polyline.shp"))

# Define bounding box for Little Loch Broom area
Wr.ext <- c(xmin = 186003.5, xmax = 209396.3, ymin = 886992.6, ymax = 899905.2)
Wr.bound <- c(xmin = 186010, xmax = 209396.3, ymin = 886992.6, ymax = 899893)

# Crop shapefiles to study area
shore.wr <- st_crop(shore, Wr.ext)
land.wr  <- st_crop(land, Wr.ext)

```


## Load 2023 Data
```{r load-2023-data}
# Load 2023 survey data
dat23 <- read.csv(here("cam_data/Wester_Ross_2023data.csv"))

# Check data structure
head(dat23)
str(dat23)
names(dat23)

######################################################## Subset and Recode Substratum Data

# Subset to records with Substratum1 classified
sub23 <- dat23 %>%
  filter(dat23$Substratum1 != "") %>%
  droplevels()

# Convert substratum columns to factors
sub23$Substratum1 <- factor(sub23$Substratum1,
                            levels = c("mud", "muddy_sand", "sand", "gravel", "cob_boulder", "rock"))
sub23$Substratum2 <- factor(sub23$Substratum2,
                            levels = c("mud", "muddy_sand", "sand", "gravel", "cob_boulder"))
sub23$Substratum3 <- factor(sub23$Substratum3,
                            levels = c("muddy_sand", "cob_boulder"))

# Summarise table counts
table(sub23$Substratum1)
table(sub23$Substratum2)
table(sub23$Substratum3)

######################################################### Convert to Spatial Object

# Convert to sf object (WGS84)
sub.sf23 <- st_as_sf(sub23, 
                     coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), remove = FALSE,
                     crs = "EPSG:4326")

# Reproject to British National Grid
sub.sf23 <- st_transform(sub.sf23, crs = "EPSG:27700")

######################################################## Add National Grid Coordinates Back to Dataframe

# Convert sf objects to data frames with National Grid x and y
sub <- as.data.frame(sub.sf)
sub23 <- as.data.frame(sub.sf23)

######################################################## Define Colour Palettes for Prediction Maps

# Define colour palettes for prediction heatmaps
couls <- rev(brewer.pal(11, "Spectral"))
couls <- c("#FFFFFF", couls)
prob.heat <- colorRampPalette(couls)

```

# functions
```{r functions}
# Function to plot base map with depth, land and rectangle
plot_base_map <- function(depth, land, Wr.bound, depth_palette) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0) + 0.1)
  plot(st_geometry(land), col = NA, border = NA)
  rect(Wr.bound["xmin"], Wr.bound["ymin"], Wr.bound["xmax"], Wr.bound["ymax"], 
       col = "lightsteelblue4", border = NA)
  plot(st_geometry(land), add = TRUE, col = 'grey40', border = 'grey60')
  plot(depth, add = TRUE, col = depth_palette(1000), legend = FALSE, axes = FALSE)
}


# Function to plot base map with no depth
plot_land <- function( land, Wr.bound, depth_palette) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0) + 0.1)
  plot(st_geometry(land), col = NA, border = NA)
  rect(Wr.bound["xmin"], Wr.bound["ymin"], Wr.bound["xmax"], Wr.bound["ymax"], 
       col = "lightsteelblue4", border = NA)
  plot(st_geometry(land), add = TRUE, col = 'grey40', border = 'grey60')
  
}





# Function to plot substratum points for a given sf object
plot_sub_points <- function(sub_sf, substratum_cols) {
  plot(st_geometry(sub_sf), pch = 19, cex = 1.5, add = TRUE,
       col = substratum_cols[as.character(sub_sf$Substratum1)])
  plot(st_geometry(sub_sf), pch = 19, cex = 1, add = TRUE,
       col = substratum_cols[as.character(sub_sf$Substratum2)])
  plot(st_geometry(sub_sf), pch = 19, cex = 0.5, add = TRUE,
       col = substratum_cols[as.character(sub_sf$Substratum3)])
}

# Function to plot substratum legend
plot_sub_legend <- function(substratum_cols) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0) + 0.1)
  plot(0, 0, type = 'n', axes = FALSE, xlab = '', ylab = '')
  legend('center',
         legend = names(substratum_cols),
         fill = substratum_cols,
         bg = 'white')
}

# Function to plot depth colour scale legend
plot_depth_legend <- function(depth, depth_palette) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0) + 0.1)
  image.plot((depth * -1),
             horizontal = FALSE,
             smallplot = c(0.6, 0.63, 0.1, 0.9),
             col = depth_palette(1000),
             legend.only = TRUE,
             axis.args = list(
               cex.axis = 1,
               at = c(0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140, 160, 180),
               labels = rev(c("0", "20", "40", "60", "80", "100", "120", "140", "160", "180")),
               tcl = 0.3, lwd = 0.5, hadj = 0.5),
             zlim = c(0, 181),
             axes = FALSE)
}

# addalpha()
addalpha <- function(colors, alpha=1.0) {
  r <- col2rgb(colors, alpha=T)
  # Apply alpha
  r[4,] <- alpha*255
  r <- r/255.0
  return(rgb(r[1,], r[2,], r[3,], r[4,]))
}

# Define substratum colours
substratum_cols <- c(
  "mud" = rgb(255,127,0, maxColorValue = 255),
  "muddy_sand" = rgb(77,175,74, maxColorValue = 255),
  "sand" = rgb(255,255,51, maxColorValue = 255),
  "gravel" = rgb(228,26,28, maxColorValue = 255),
  "cob_boulder" = rgb(152,78,163, maxColorValue = 255),
  "rock" = rgb(55,126,184, maxColorValue = 255)
)

```

# K-fold cross validation
```{r}



K <- 5
N <- 100
first.run <- TRUE

# Your k-fold splitting function (unchanged)
kfoldSplit <- function(x, k=K, train=TRUE){
  x <- sample(x, size = length(x), replace = FALSE)
  out <- suppressWarnings(split(x, factor(1:k)))
  if(train) out <- lapply(out, function(x, len) (1:len)[-x], len=length(unlist(out)))
  return(out)
}

kfolds <- kfoldSplit(1:nrow(sub), k = K, train = TRUE)

# Sediment types
sediments <- c("mud", "muddy_sand", "sand", "gravel", "cob_boulder", "rock")

# Initialize list to store RMSE matrices per sediment
evalList <- lapply(sediments, function(x) matrix(NA, nrow = K, ncol = 1, dimnames = list(1:K, "GAM")))
names(evalList) <- sediments

for (run in 1:N) {
  
  for (i in 1:K) {
    
    cat("Run", run, "- K-fold", i, "of", K, "...\n")
    
    idx <- kfolds[[i]]
    idxBool <- (1:nrow(sub)) %in% idx
    
    for (sed in sediments) {
      # Observed test values
      obs.test <- sub[!idxBool, sed]
      
      # Fit GAM on training data
      GAM <- gam(
        formula = as.formula(paste(sed, "~ s(Longitude, Latitude) + s(Depth)")),
        data = sub.sf[idx, ],
        family = binomial
      )
      
      # Predict on test data
      pred.test <- predict(GAM, newdata = sub.sf[!idxBool, ], type = "response")
      
      # Calculate RMSE and store
      rmse <- sqrt(mean((pred.test - obs.test)^2))
      evalList[[sed]][i, "GAM"] <- rmse
    }
    
  }
  
  # Combine evaluation results for all sediments
  evals.tmp <- do.call(rbind, evalList)
  
  if (first.run) {
    evals <- evals.tmp
    first.run <- FALSE
  } else {
    evals <- rbind(evals, evals.tmp)
  }
  
  print(evals)
}


round(apply(evals,2,FUN = function(x, na.rm=TRUE) c(mean(x,na.rm=TRUE), sd(x, na.rm=TRUE))),3)


```


# accuracy curve across probabilities
```{r}
par(op)

# Clean Substratum columns
True.dat <- sub.sf23
substratum.cols <- c("Substratum1", "Substratum2", "Substratum3")


# safely convert NAs to "No" in Substratum columns
for (col in substratum.cols) {
  True.dat[[col]] <- as.character(True.dat[[col]])
  True.dat[[col]][is.na(True.dat[[col]])] <- "No"
}



# Substratum labels and raster stack
substrata <- c("mud", "muddy_sand", "sand", "gravel", "cob_boulder", "rock")
sub.stack <- rast(list(mud.r, muddyS.r, sand.r, gravel.r, cob.r, rock.r))
sub.trim <- classify(sub.stack, cbind(0, NA))  # set 0 to NA

# Build truth dataframe: Yes/No for each substratum type
truth <- sapply(substrata, function(sed) {
  apply(True.dat[, substratum.cols], 1, function(row) {
    if (any(trimws(row) == sed)) "Yes" else "No"
  })
})
colnames(truth) <- substrata
truth.sp <- sub.sf23

# Probability thresholds
p.vals <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.01)

# Initialise list to hold accuracy values
overall.acc <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(p.vals), ncol = length(substrata))
colnames(overall.acc) <- substrata

# Loop through substratum layers
for (k in seq_along(substrata)) {
  cat("Processing:", substrata[k], "\n")
  
  layer.trim <- sub.trim[[k]]
  
  acc.vals <- numeric(length(p.vals))
  
  for (i in seq_along(p.vals)) {
    # Apply threshold
    pred.layer <- classify(layer.trim, cbind(-Inf, p.vals[i], NA))
    
    # Extract prediction values at sample points
    pred.prob <- extract(pred.layer, truth.sp)
    
    # Convert to binary: 1 if non-NA, 0 if NA
    pred.bin <- ifelse(!is.na(pred.prob[,2]), "Yes", "No")
    
    # Accuracy: proportion correct
    acc <- mean(pred.bin == truth[,k], na.rm = TRUE)
    acc.vals[i] <- acc
  }
  
  overall.acc[,k] <- acc.vals
}

# Mean and CI across substrata (per threshold)
acc.comb <- rowMeans(overall.acc)
acc.sd <- apply(overall.acc, 1, sd)
acc.up <- acc.comb + (acc.sd / sqrt(length(substrata)) * 1.96)
acc.lo <- acc.comb - (acc.sd / sqrt(length(substrata)) * 1.96)

# Plot results
plot(p.vals, acc.comb, type='l', ylim=c(0,1), lwd=3, xlim=c(0,1.1), xlab="Probability Threshold", ylab="Accuracy")
lines(p.vals, acc.up, lty=2, lwd=2)
lines(p.vals, acc.lo, lty=2, lwd=2)
for (j in 1:ncol(overall.acc)) {
  lines(p.vals, overall.acc[,j], col=substratum_cols[j], lwd=2)
  best.i <- which.max(overall.acc[,j])
  points(p.vals[best.i], overall.acc[best.i,j], pch=18, cex=2, col=substratum_cols[j])
  text(p.vals[best.i]+0.02, overall.acc[best.i,j]+0.03, labels=round(overall.acc[best.i,j], 2), col=substratum_cols[j])
}

# Add overall max point
best.overall <- which.max(acc.comb)
points(p.vals[best.overall], acc.comb[best.overall], pch=18, cex=3)
text(p.vals[best.overall]+0.05, acc.comb[best.overall]+0.05, labels=round(acc.comb[best.overall], 2))

legend('bottomright', legend=substrata, fill=substratum_cols, bg='white')

# AUC calculations
auc.comb <- flux::auc(p.vals, acc.comb)
auc.indiv <- sapply(1:ncol(overall.acc), function(x) flux::auc(p.vals, overall.acc[,x]))

# Best thresholds per substratum
best.thresholds <- p.vals[apply(overall.acc, 2, which.max)]
names(best.thresholds) <- substrata

# Summaries
cat("\nMean optimal threshold:", mean(best.thresholds), "\n")
cat("Mean AUC:", mean(auc.indiv), "\n")
auc.indiv



#######################
# Estimate finite difference derivative
acc.diff <- diff(acc.comb) / diff(p.vals)

# Find index where derivative is closest to 1
target.i <- which.min(abs(acc.diff - 1))

# Get corresponding threshold and accuracy
target.threshold <- p.vals[target.i]
target.acc <- acc.comb[target.i]

# Plot point on curve
points(target.threshold, target.acc, pch=8, col="red", cex=2)
text(target.threshold+0.02, target.acc+0.04, 
     labels=paste0("dA/dT ≈ 1 @ T=", round(target.threshold, 2)), col="red", cex=0.9)

# Report result
cat("At threshold ≈", round(target.threshold, 3), "slope ≈ 1 and accuracy ≈", round(target.acc, 3), "\n")


for (j in 1:ncol(overall.acc)) {
  acc.diff <- diff(overall.acc[,j]) / diff(p.vals)
  target.i <- which.min(abs(acc.diff - 1))
  
  points(p.vals[target.i], overall.acc[target.i, j], pch=4, col=substratum_cols[j], cex=1.5)
  text(p.vals[target.i]+0.015, overall.acc[target.i, j]-0.03,
       labels=paste0("T=", round(p.vals[target.i],2)), col=substratum_cols[j], cex=0.8)
}


```


# fitted with smoothers for easier graph
```{r}
dev.off()

# Fit a smoothing spline to the accuracy vs threshold curve
spline.fit <- smooth.spline(p.vals, acc.comb, spar=0.7)

# Predict derivative (1st derivative) at all thresholds
spline.deriv <- predict(spline.fit, p.vals, deriv=1)

# Find where derivative is closest to 1
target.i <- which.min(abs(spline.deriv$y - 1))
target.threshold <- p.vals[target.i]
target.acc <- predict(spline.fit, target.threshold)$y

# Plot mean accuracy curve
plot(p.vals, acc.comb, type='l', ylim=c(0,1), lwd=3, xlim=c(0,1.1),
     xlab="Probability Threshold", ylab="Accuracy")
lines(p.vals, acc.up, lty=2, lwd=2)
lines(p.vals, acc.lo, lty=2, lwd=2)
lines(spline.fit, col="blue", lwd=2)

# Add point where slope ≈ 1
points(target.threshold, target.acc, pch=8, col="red", cex=2)
text(target.threshold+0.02, target.acc+0.04, 
     labels=paste0("Slope ≈ 1 @ T=", round(target.threshold, 2)), col="red", cex=0.9)

# Optional: plot derivative curve for reference
plot(p.vals, spline.deriv$y, type='l', col="darkgreen", lwd=2,
     xlab="Threshold", ylab="d(Accuracy)/d(Threshold)",
     main="Derivative of Accuracy vs Threshold")
abline(h=1, lty=2, col="red")
abline(v=target.threshold, lty=3, col="grey")
points(target.threshold, spline.deriv$y[target.i], pch=8, col="red", cex=2)

####

# Plot base: mean accuracy and CI
plot(p.vals, acc.comb, type='l', ylim=c(0,1), lwd=3, xlim=c(0,1.1),
     xlab="Probability Threshold", ylab="Accuracy")
lines(p.vals, acc.up, lty=2, lwd=2)
lines(p.vals, acc.lo, lty=2, lwd=2)

# Storage vectors
slope1.thresholds <- numeric(ncol(overall.acc))
slope1.accs <- numeric(ncol(overall.acc))

# Loop through each substratum
for (j in 1:ncol(overall.acc)) {
  
  # Fit smoothing spline for substratum j
  spline.fit <- smooth.spline(p.vals, overall.acc[,j], spar=0.7)
  
  # Predict first derivative
  spline.deriv <- predict(spline.fit, p.vals, deriv=1)
  
  # Find where derivative ≈ 1
  target.i <- which.min(abs(spline.deriv$y - 1))
  target.threshold <- p.vals[target.i]
  target.acc <- predict(spline.fit, target.threshold)$y
  
  # Store values
  slope1.thresholds[j] <- target.threshold
  slope1.accs[j] <- target.acc
  
  # Plot substratum accuracy curve
  lines(p.vals, overall.acc[,j], col=substratum_cols[j], lwd=2)
  
  # Plot point at max accuracy
  best.i <- which.max(overall.acc[,j])
  points(p.vals[best.i], overall.acc[best.i,j], pch=18, cex=2, col=substratum_cols[j])
  
  # Plot slope ≈ 1 point
  points(target.threshold, target.acc, pch=8, col=substratum_cols[j], cex=2)
  
  # Label slope ≈ 1 point
  text(target.threshold+0.02, target.acc+0.03, 
       labels=paste0("T=", round(target.threshold, 2)), col=substratum_cols[j], cex=0.8)
}

# Optional: Print thresholds and accuracies where slope ≈ 1 for each substratum
slope1.thresholds
slope1.accs
```

# combined map with informed thresholds
```{r combined map}

slope1.thresholds <- c(0.1, 0.27, 0.12, 0.10, 0.17, 0.09)  # example values

# Name rasters and matching thresholds in a named list
substratum_rasters <- list(
  mud = mud.r,
  muddy_sand = muddyS.r,
  sand = sand.r,
  gravel = gravel.r,
  cob_boulder = cob.r,
  rock = rock.r
)

# Apply optimal threshold trimming
substratum_trimmed <- mapply(function(raster, thresh) {
  raster[raster < thresh] <- NA
  return(raster)
}, substratum_rasters, slope1.thresholds, SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

# Now assign each back to a clean named object
mud.trim         <- substratum_trimmed$mud
muddy_sand.trim  <- substratum_trimmed$muddy_sand
sand.trim        <- substratum_trimmed$sand
```
